claim_summary: MAS4TS contributes a temporal visual-reasoning and latent reconstruction mechanism, shared agent memory, and task-routed tool-chain execution with verification for forecasting, classification, imputation, and anomaly detection.

claim_evidence.quote: Based on this insight, we propose MAS4TS, the first tool-driven Multi-Agent System for general Time Series analysis, built upon an Analyzer–Reasoner–Executor paradigm.
Specifically, MAS4TS performs visual reasoning directly on time series plots using VLMs to obtain structured anchors, which subsequently guide trajectory reconstruction in latent space.

modules.name: Plot-anchor and latent-trajectory reasoning
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK no: sparse visual anchors and latent trajectory reconstruction are not defined by one output objective and support multiple task families. R3_2 GTS yes: it operates on ordered series and reconstructs a temporally coherent latent trajectory. Counterfactual: changing task outputs does not require redesigning its temporal plot-to-trajectory mechanism.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - shared temporal reasoning across tasks
R3_2_GTS:yes - plot anchors guide temporal trajectory reconstruction
R4:Interface and Interaction; Tools and Execution

evidence.quote: The Reasoner aims to bridge intuitive visual pattern recognition and precise numerical inference for time series analysis.
we introduce a latent construction module that reconstructs a continuous latent trajectory by treating anchors as conditioning signals that guide latent-space evolution.
MAS4TS provides a unified agent-driven framework that shares common perception, reasoning, and memory components across these tasks.

modules.name: Confidence-gated shared agent memory
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK no: this exchanges agent states without embedding a task output criterion. R3_2 GTS no: the shared matrix coordinates agent hidden states but does not impose temporal ordering, windows, frequency, units, or information availability. R3_3 GH yes: it manages execution state and inter-agent coordination. Counterfactual: its mechanism need not be redesigned when changing task families.
rubric_path: R3_2_GTS:no - no temporal semantics in the memory update criterion
R4:Memory and Context; Planning and Orchestration

evidence.quote: We define a set of agents {Agent(i) }N i=1 for batch data processing, where in our instantiation N =3 corresponds to Analyzer, Reasoner, and Executor.
Cross-agent coordination is achieved through a shared memory matrix M ∈ RL×dm , which integrates knowledge across agents via gated fusion.

modules.name: Task-routed tool chains and result verification
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK yes: the router conditions on task type and chooses task-specific chains, while the verifier applies task-specific consistency criteria. Counterfactual: changing the task family requires changing tool-chain semantics and validation objectives. R3_2/R3_3 are not selected because the core procedure embeds task objectives.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - task-conditioned chains and verifier criteria
R4:Planning and Orchestration; Tools and Execution

evidence.quote: At execution time, an adaptive router selects a tool chain from a predefined library T = {T1 , . . . , TM }, where each tool implements a specialized operation (e.g., trend extrapolation, decomposition, smoothing, statistical prediction, constraint projection, and residual correction).

To ensure numerical validity and task consistency, MAS4TS employs a lightweight verifier that performs: (i) format and shape correction, (ii) constraint validation, and (iii) task-specific normalization.
